access: Anonymous HTTPS GET/POST to the public ArcGIS REST query endpoint, at most one request per second per host, no token or cookie. Only object-ID, native-ID and county/town scope fields were ever requested; no owner, address, sale, account or taxpayer fields.
helperScripts: tmp/adapter-staging/us-statewide-a/scripts/ (state-cities.py, polite.mjs, meta.mjs, uniqueness.mjs, statewide-repeats.mjs, coverage.mjs, blank-breakdown.mjs, dup-ids.mjs, repeat-geometry.mjs, distinct-area-repeats.mjs, parts-overlap.mjs, verify.mjs, verify-parts.mjs, dense-cell.mjs, descriptors.mjs)
heldReason: Endpoint already catalogued as us-co-oit-public-parcels-denver (attributeFilters countyName=Denver, idField parcel_id, idPrefix US-CO-). A statewide discovery profile on that entry would probe every Colorado city through a Denver-only filter, and widening it in place would change identity (countyName must join parcel_id) and therefore every existing Denver parcel ID. Caller decision needed: a separate statewide entry on the same endpoint (candidate below, live-verified) or a migration of the Denver entry.

layer.description: The spatial polygon data is aggregated by the State of Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology Geospatial Information Systems Team. This dataset represents an on-going relationship between the counties, municipalities and the State of Colorado to provide accurate updated land parcel information. Updates are collected annually.
layer.copyrightText: This dataset is created and maintained by the Governor's Office of Information Technology (OIT) GIS Team; sourced data is provided by various county, regional, and local government entities.

coverage.note: Missing counties derived from the live countyName groups (44 present); the service description says updates are collected annually from participating counties. All five uncovered UN cities (Denver, Fort Collins, Greeley, Boulder, Longmont) lie in present counties.

identity.why: parcel_id is county-scoped (the existing Denver entry fixes the county for this reason), so countyName is joined. No GlobalID; account is an assessor account field and is not requested.

uniqueness.result: Denver and Weld: no repeated parcel_id. Larimer (1,133 IDs) and Boulder (834 IDs) publish one parcel_id on several non-overlapping polygons plus stacked identical copies (up to 487 rows), hence parts mode; disjointParts rejected for the same stacked-copy reason as Ohio. Distinct parcel_ids share identical polygons (25 in the Fort Collins bbox).

candidateDescriptor.name: Colorado Public Parcels (OIT statewide composite)
candidateDescriptor.operator: Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology (OIT) GIS, from county and municipal parcel data
candidateDescriptor.scope: OIT statewide composite of 44 of 64 Colorado counties (2,600,023 rows on 2026-10-12). Canonical identity is countyName plus the county parcel_id; same-key rows form one native parcel group. Rows without parcel_id (5,310) are excluded.
caveats: Absent counties: Alamosa, Baca, Bent, Chaffee, Cheyenne, Conejos, Costilla, Crowley, Delta, Fremont, Jackson, Kiowa, Kit Carson, Las Animas, Lincoln, Mineral, Montrose, Otero, Phillips, Prowers.
parcel_id is county-scoped (the Denver entry fixes countyName for this reason), so identity is the composite countyName~parcel_id.

Larimer (1,133 IDs) and Boulder (834 IDs) publish one parcel_id on several polygons plus stacked byte-identical copies (up to 487 rows); all components are fetched and unioned. disjointParts is off because stacked copies fail the overlap check (Boulder 146329311017 failed with it on); sampled distinct components did not overlap.
Distinct parcel_ids can share one identical polygon (stacked condominium units; 25 shared polygons in one 0.01 degree Fort Collins box).
candidateDescriptor.attribution: Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology GIS and contributing counties. Adapted to WGS84.
candidateDescriptor.licenceNote: Source conditions are informational; users choose their source and intended use.

jurisdiction.basis: OIT aggregates county and municipal parcels into one statewide layer, but only 44 of 64 counties are present; cities in the 20 absent counties cannot qualify.
